record.passage: At the start of senior high, the student felt (1) ______ about every new subject. It was her teacher who helped her become more (2) ______ step by step. The student was (3) ______ about everything around her, so she asked many questions in class. Her deskmate（同桌）, a classmate who was always (4) ______, never forgot（忘记） to bring notes for her. The student was (5) ______ to enter a top university, and she worked hard every day. She wanted to (6) ______ her dream through steady effort. At first it was hard for her to (7) ______ to the fast pace（步伐） of school life. Her parents would (8) ______ her whenever she felt tired. Her teacher was able to (9) ______ her to join the school debate club, and she slowly learned to (10) ______ on her studies instead of worrying. (11) ______, she became calmer and more sure of herself. If she had not met such a patient teacher, she would not have (12) ______ found her own way. Now she can study (13) ______ and face problems on her own. Looking back, she knows that true (14) ______ comes from small daily progress. She hopes that every student should have the (15) ______ to grow at their own speed.

questions.stem: Choose the best word for blank (1).
questions.explanation: 新学期开始学生对每门新科目感到焦虑，与后文老师帮助她变得自信形成对比。proud（骄傲）和calm（平静）与“需要帮助”的语境矛盾。
knowledge_points: At the start of senior high, the student felt (1) ______ about every new subject.
后文说老师帮她逐步改变，说明起初是负面情绪，anxious最合适。
questions.context_clue: At the start of senior high, the student felt (1) ______ about every new subject.
questions.clue_argument: 后文说老师帮她逐步改变，说明起初是负面情绪，anxious最合适。

questions.stem: Choose the best word for blank (2).
questions.explanation: 老师帮助学生逐步变得更自信，与开头焦虑形成成长对比。silent（沉默）和angry（生气）不符合“帮助成长”的积极方向。
knowledge_points: It was her teacher who helped her become more (2) ______ step by step.
help sb become more... 表示积极变化，confident符合成长主题。
questions.context_clue: It was her teacher who helped her become more (2) ______ step by step.
questions.clue_argument: help sb become more... 表示积极变化，confident符合成长主题。

so she asked many questions 是结果，说明原因是curious。

questions.clue_argument: so she asked many questions 是结果，说明原因是curious。

never forgot to bring notes 体现可靠，reliable最贴切。

questions.clue_argument: never forgot（忘记） to bring notes 体现可靠，reliable最贴切。

enter a top university 与 work hard 表明她有志向，ambitious合适。

questions.clue_argument: enter a top university 与 work hard 表明她有志向，ambitious合适。

knowledge_points: She wanted to (6) ______ her dream through steady effort.
through steady effort 指向实现梦想，achieve her dream最自然。
questions.context_clue: She wanted to (6) ______ her dream through steady effort.
questions.clue_argument: through steady effort 指向实现梦想，achieve her dream最自然。

questions.stem: Choose the best word for blank (7).

whenever she felt tired 需要正面支持，encourage最合适。

pro_audit.coherence_reason: The passage is a connected narrative about a student's growth from anxiety to confidence with support from teacher, deskmate, and parents.

questions.reason: The context of starting senior high and feeling about new subjects suggests anxiety, which aligns with the later help from the teacher.
The teacher helped her become more confident, which contrasts with her initial anxiety and fits the positive growth narrative.
Asking many questions in class indicates curiosity about everything around her.
A deskmate who never forgets to bring notes is reliable, and the other options do not fit the described behavior.
Wanting to enter a top university and working hard every day indicates ambition.
The phrase 'achieve her dream' is a common collocation meaning to realize one's dream.
The phrase 'adapt to' means to adjust to something, which fits the fast pace of school life.
Parents would encourage her when she felt tired, which is a supportive action.
The teacher persuaded her to join the debate club, meaning the teacher convinced her to do it.
The phrase 'concentrate on' means to focus attention on something, which fits with studies.
The word 'gradually' fits the context of slow change over time, as indicated by 'slowly learned'.
The word 'eventually' means in the end, which fits the hypothetical situation of finding her own way.
The phrase 'on her own' suggests independence, so 'independently' is the best fit.
True confidence comes from small daily progress, which aligns with the theme of self-growth.
The phrase 'opportunity to grow' is a natural collocation meaning a chance to develop.

record.passage: Last term, the student faced a new digital learning platform（平台）（平台）for the first time. She felt (1) anxious because she could not follow the online lessons at first. Her teacher told her that anyone could become (2) confident with daily practice. A classmate, who was always (3) curious about new apps, showed her how to use the search tool. The platform（平台） was not always (4) reliable, so the student learned to save her work often. If she were more (5) ambitious, she would try the extra tasks every week. Only by planning her time well could she (6) achieve real progress. Her teacher suggested that she (7) adapt her study habits to the online setting. Students were (8) encouraged to ask questions in the chat room. Last month, the student (9) persuaded her parents to let her study at home on rainy days. If she (10) concentrated for forty minutes, she took a short break. By (11) gradually building good habits, she improved her grades. Her teacher insisted that she (12) eventually set a clear goal for each week. With her teacher (13) independently checking her progress, she felt safe. Now she has (14) confidence in her ability, and every lesson is a new (15) opportunity to learn.

record.passage: Last summer, my cousin and I travelled to Xi'an by train. It was not the famous terracotta（陶土） warriors（武士） that impressed us most — it was the journey itself. ①____ was the slow overnight（通宵） train that gave us time to talk with strangers. ②____ we enjoyed most was the view of the yellow river at sunrise（日出）. It was only after we arrived ③____ we realised how much we had learned on the road. Since then, we ④____ many trips together. Last month, while we ⑤____ a map at the station, a kind old man showed us a shortcut（捷径）. We ⑥____ to that city three times by now. The number of tourists ⑦____ growing every year, and neither my cousin nor I ⑧____ tired of travelling. Each of our trips ⑨____ something new. For us, travel is ⑩____ education that never ends.

questions.stem: Choose the best word for blank ①.
questions.explanation: 此处是强调句 It was ... that ...，强调主语 the slow overnight（通宵） train，故用 It。That 和 This 不能引导强调句结构，There 与 was 搭配不构成强调句。
questions.evidence_sentence: It was not the famous terracotta（陶土） warriors（武士） that impressed us most — it was the journey itself.
questions.context_clue: ①____ was the slow overnight（通宵） train that gave us time to talk with strangers.
questions.clue_argument: 强调句结构 It was ... that ... 需要 It 作形式主语。

questions.stem: Choose the best word for blank ②.
questions.explanation: 此处是主语从句，从句缺少 enjoyed 的宾语，用 What 引导，意为“我们最享受的东西”。That 在主语从句中不作成分，Which 需要先行范围，It 不能引导从句。
questions.evidence_sentence: It was the view of the yellow river at sunrise（日出） that we enjoyed most.
questions.context_clue: ②____ we enjoyed most was the view of the yellow river at sunrise（日出）.
questions.clue_argument: 从句缺宾语，需用 What 引导主语从句。

questions.stem: Choose the best word for blank ③.
questions.explanation: 此处是强调句 It was only after we arrived that we realised...，强调时间状语，用 that。which 不能用于强调句，when 和 where 会与 after 重复或造成结构错误。
questions.evidence_sentence: It was only after we arrived that we realised how much we had learned on the road.
questions.context_clue: It was only after we arrived ③____ we realised how much we had learned on the road.
questions.clue_argument: 强调句 It was ... that ... 中连接词固定用 that。

questions.stem: Choose the best form for blank ④.
questions.explanation: Since then 表示从过去到现在，主句用现在完成时 have taken。took 只表过去，had taken 表过去完成，take 表一般现在，均与 since then 不符。
questions.evidence_sentence: Since then, we have taken many trips together.
questions.context_clue: Since then, we ④____ many trips together.
questions.clue_argument: Since then 提示现在完成时。

questions.stem: Choose the best form for blank ⑤.
questions.explanation: while 引导的从句表示过去某时正在进行的动作，用过去进行时 were reading。read 一般过去时不能体现“正在”，have read 和 are reading 时态与 Last month 不符。
questions.evidence_sentence: Last month, while we were reading a map at the station, a kind old man showed us a shortcut（捷径）.
questions.context_clue: Last month, while we ⑤____ a map at the station, a kind old man showed us a shortcut（捷径）.
questions.clue_argument: while 加过去时间，表示过去正在进行，用过去进行时。

questions.stem: Choose the best form for blank ⑥.
questions.explanation: by now 表示到现在为止，用现在完成时 have been。went 只表过去，had been 表过去完成，go 表一般现在，均与 by now 不符。
questions.evidence_sentence: We have been to that city three times by now.
questions.context_clue: We ⑥____ to that city three times by now.
questions.clue_argument: by now 提示现在完成时。

questions.stem: Choose the best form for blank ⑦.
questions.explanation: The number of ... 作主语时谓语用单数，故用 is。are 和 were 是复数形式，have 不能与 growing 构成进行时。
questions.evidence_sentence: The number of tourists is growing every year.
questions.context_clue: The number of tourists ⑦____ growing every year.
questions.clue_argument: The number of 加复数名词，谓语用单数。

questions.stem: Choose the best form for blank ⑧.
questions.explanation: neither ... nor ... 连接主语时遵循就近原则，靠近谓语的是 I，故用 am。is 和 are 与 I 不一致，be 不能单独作谓语。
questions.evidence_sentence: Neither my cousin nor I am tired of travelling.
questions.context_clue: neither my cousin nor I ⑧____ tired of travelling.
questions.clue_argument: neither...nor... 就近原则，靠近 I，用 am。

questions.stem: Choose the best form for blank ⑨.
questions.explanation: Each of ... 作主语时谓语用单数，且表示一般事实，用 brings。bring 是复数形式，brought 时态不符，bringing 不能单独作谓语。
questions.evidence_sentence: Each of our trips brings something new.
questions.context_clue: Each of our trips ⑨____ something new.
questions.clue_argument: Each of 加复数名词，谓语用单数。

questions.stem: Choose the best word for blank ⑩.
questions.explanation: education 在此为抽象名词具体化，表示“一种教育”，且 education 以元音音素开头，用 an。a 用于辅音音素前，the 表特指，不填则缺少冠词。
questions.evidence_sentence: For us, travel is an education that never ends.
questions.context_clue: For us, travel is ⑩____ education that never ends.
questions.clue_argument: education 以元音音素开头，表示“一种教育”，用 an。

record.passage: Every year, millions of tons of plastic waste enter the ocean. This pollution harms sea animals and birds. Many fish eat tiny pieces of plastic, and then larger animals eat those fish. The plastic moves up the food chain and can even reach our dinner tables. Scientists have found plastic in the stomachs of whales and sea turtles（海龟）. They warn that this problem is growing. However, there is hope. Some countries have started to reduce single-use（一次性） plastics. For example, many shops no longer offer free plastic bags. People are encouraged to bring their own bags when shopping. Schools are also teaching students about the importance（重要性） of recycling. A student named Li Hua started a recycling club at her school. She and her classmates collect plastic bottles and send them to a recycling centre. Their efforts have reduced waste by 30 per cent. Li Hua says, 'Small actions can make a big difference.' The fight against ocean plastic is not easy, but everyone can help. By using less plastic and recycling more, we can protect our oceans for future generations.

record.passage:
Food is more than something we eat; it is a language that tells the story of a place and its people. In China, this language changes from north to south. A visitor to Beijing may notice that wheat, not rice, shapes the daily table. There, a cook turns flour（面粉） into dumplings, noodles and pancakes, and the smell of hot pot fills the streets on cold evenings. In the south, where heavy rain feeds the fields, rice becomes the centre of almost every meal. What people choose to cook, therefore, often depends on what the land can grow.

Food also carries culture across borders. When Chinese families moved abroad, they took their recipes with them. In a foreign city, a small restaurant may serve noodles that taste exactly like home, and customers from many backgrounds come to share them. These dishes, which once belonged to one village, now belong to the world. This is how tradition survives: it travels, it mixes, and it grows.

Perhaps the most important lesson is that sharing food builds friendship. A simple bowl of soup, offered with a smile, can say more than words. Whether it is dumplings in the north or rice in the south, the meal is never only about taste. It is about memory, family and the warm feeling of being welcome at someone's table.

record.passage: When the student first read about climate change, she felt worried but also far away from the problem. Her teacher, however, asked the class to think about one simple question: what can we do today? The student decided to act. She started a small group with a classmate, and they planned to make their school greener. At first, they only collected paper for recycling. Then they noticed that the lights in empty classrooms were often left on. They wrote a short report and gave it to the school office. The office agreed to let students check the lights each afternoon. In just one month, the school used less electricity. The student also spoke（辐条） to younger children about turning off taps and not wasting food. She explained that small actions, when many people do them together, can have a big effect. Her teacher was proud of the group and said their work showed real purpose. The student learned that climate action does not always begin with governments or big companies. It can begin with a student, a classmate, and a teacher who care enough to start.

record.passage: In today's classrooms, AI tools are becoming common. The student uses an AI app to practise（练习） English. Her teacher, who has studied technology in education, explains that AI can offer quick feedback（反馈）. A classmate, however, worries that students might depend on AI too much. Last month, the student used an AI writing helper to check her essay. The app suggested many changes, and she accepted them without thinking. Her teacher noticed this and said, "If you always accept AI's advice without question, you will not develop your own ability." The student realised her mistake. She now uses AI only to check grammar and vocabulary. She writes her first draft alone, then asks the app for ideas. The teacher is pleased with this balanced approach. She believes that AI should be a tool, not a master. The classmate agrees and says, "We should use AI to help us learn, not to do the learning for us." The school has started a club where students discuss how to use AI wisely. The student joined the club and now helps others. She feels more confident in her learning. AI is powerful, but human judgment is still the key.

record.passage:
Why do we sleep? For years, scientists have studied this question, and their findings are surprising. The brain does not simply shut down at night. Instead, it works hard to sort and store the day's experiences. According to recent research, sleep helps us remember what we have learned and prepares us for new challenges.

A student named Li Hua once believed that staying up late was the best way to prepare for exams. He drank（喝） coffee and studied until 2 a.m（米）. every night. After two weeks, his grades dropped, and he felt awful. His teacher advised him to change his habit. She explained that the brain needs sleep to turn short-term（短期） memories into long-term（长期） ones. If he had slept well, he would have remembered more.

Now Li Hua goes to bed before eleven. He keeps his phone away from his bed and avoids bright screens. He also takes a short walk after dinner. These simple habits have made a big difference. His energy has improved, and his test scores are rising.

Sleep is not a waste of time. It is a basic need, like food and water. Teenagers need about nine hours of sleep each night, yet many get far less. Scientists warn that a lack of sleep can harm memory, mood（心情）, and health. So the next question is simple: are you getting enough sleep?

questions.stem: What can we infer about Li Hua from the passage?
options: He no longer studies for exams.
He has learned that good sleep supports his learning.
He still believes staying up late is helpful.

Her teacher, Ms. Chen, often reminded the members that small actions could make a big difference. ① the club began, the student had never thought about helping others in her neighbourhood. Now she spends two hours every Saturday ② rubbish in the park with her classmates. If she ③ more free time, she would organise more activities. She wishes she ④ more people to join them. Ms. Chen suggests that every member ⑤ at least one new volunteer each month. It is important that the club ⑥ its plans clearly to the public. The student's classmate, Li Ming, insisted that everyone ⑦ on time for the weekend project. Only by working together ⑧ real change happen. Not only ⑨ the volunteers clean the park, but they also teach children about recycling. Such is the power of community service ⑩ it brings neighbours closer. The student feels proud of what they have achieved.

questions.stem: ① ___ the club began, the student had never thought about helping others in her neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: 从句表示“在俱乐部开始之前”，主句用过去完成时，动作先后关系清晰，故用Before。After和Since都表示“之后/自从”，与“从未想过”的过去完成时逻辑矛盾。
questions.evidence_sentence: ① the club began, the student had never thought about helping others in her neighbourhood.
questions.context_clue: the student had never thought about helping others
questions.clue_argument: 过去完成时表示在俱乐部开始前从未想过，需用Before引导时间状语从句。

questions.stem: Now she spends two hours every Saturday ② rubbish in the park with her classmates.
questions.explanation: spend time doing sth.是固定搭配，表示“花费时间做某事”，故用动名词collecting。collect和to collect均不符合spend time后的搭配，collected为过去分词也不正确。
questions.evidence_sentence: Now she spends two hours every Saturday ② rubbish in the park with her classmates.
questions.context_clue: spends two hours every Saturday
questions.clue_argument: spend time doing sth.结构要求动名词。

questions.stem: If she ③ more free time, she would organise more activities.
questions.explanation: 主句用would organise，说明是与现在事实相反的虚拟条件句，if从句用一般过去时had。has和will have用于真实条件句，would have不能出现在if从句中表示与现在相反。
questions.evidence_sentence: If she ③ more free time, she would organise more activities.
questions.context_clue: she would organise more activities
questions.clue_argument: 主句would do提示if从句用一般过去时构成虚拟。

questions.stem: She wishes she ④ more people to join them.
questions.explanation: wish后接宾语从句表示与现在事实相反的愿望时，从句用一般过去时，情态动词用could。can persuade和will persuade表示真实可能，persuades时态不符。
questions.evidence_sentence: She wishes she ④ more people to join them.
questions.context_clue: She wishes
questions.clue_argument: wish后的虚拟从句用过去时或could do表示现在愿望。

questions.stem: Ms. Chen suggests that every member ⑤ at least one new volunteer each month.
questions.explanation: suggest表示“建议”时，其后that从句用虚拟语气，谓语用(should) do，故用动词原形invite。invites和invited不是虚拟形式，will invite也不符合。
questions.evidence_sentence: Ms. Chen suggests that every member ⑤ at least one new volunteer each month.
questions.context_clue: suggests that every member
questions.clue_argument: suggest表建议时从句谓语用should加动词原形，should可省略。

questions.stem: It is important that the club ⑥ its plans clearly to the public.
questions.explanation: It is important that...句型中从句用虚拟语气，谓语用(should) do，故用动词原形state。states和is stating不是虚拟形式，stated时态也不符合。
questions.evidence_sentence: It is important that the club ⑥ its plans clearly to the public.
questions.context_clue: It is important that the club
questions.clue_argument: It is important that从句需用should加动词原形，should省略。

questions.stem: The student's classmate, Li Ming, insisted that everyone ⑦ on time for the weekend project.
questions.explanation: insist表示“坚持要求”时，从句用虚拟语气(should) do，故用动词原形arrive。arrives和will arrive不是虚拟形式，arrived时态不符。
questions.evidence_sentence: The student's classmate, Li Ming, insisted that everyone ⑦ on time for the weekend project.
questions.context_clue: insisted that everyone
questions.clue_argument: insist表坚持要求时从句用should加动词原形，should省略。

questions.stem: Only by working together ⑧ real change happen.
questions.explanation: Only加状语位于句首时，主句用部分倒装，情态动词can提到主语前，构成can real change happen。could时态不符，does和will不能与happen构成正确搭配。
questions.evidence_sentence: Only by working together ⑧ real change happen.
questions.context_clue: Only by working together
questions.clue_argument: Only加方式状语置于句首，主句需部分倒装，情态动词提前。

questions.stem: Not only ⑨ the volunteers clean the park, but they also teach children about recycling.
questions.explanation: Not only位于句首时，前一分句用部分倒装，实义动词clean需借助助动词do，构成do the volunteers clean。did时态与后文teach不一致，are和have不能与clean构成正确结构。
questions.evidence_sentence: Not only ⑨ the volunteers clean the park, but they also teach children about recycling.
questions.context_clue: Not only ... but they also teach
questions.clue_argument: Not only置于句首，前句部分倒装，一般现在时用助动词do。

questions.stem: Such is the power of community service ⑩ it brings neighbours closer.
questions.explanation: Such is...that...是such置于句首引起的倒装结构，that引导结果状语从句。as和which不能与such is构成结果状语从句，what不能引导该从句。
questions.evidence_sentence: Such is the power of community service ⑩ it brings neighbours closer.
questions.context_clue: Such is the power of community service
questions.clue_argument: Such is...that...固定结构，that引导结果状语从句。

The fixed phrase 'spend time doing something' requires the gerund 'collecting'.
The main clause 'would organise' signals a second conditional, requiring the past simple 'had' in the if-clause.
After 'wish' for a present unreal situation, 'could' is the correct modal verb.
The verb 'suggest' triggers the subjunctive mood, requiring the base form 'invite'.
The structure 'It is important that' requires the subjunctive mood, using the base form 'state'.
The verb 'insisted' (meaning demanded) requires the subjunctive mood, using the base form 'arrive'.
The inversion after 'Only by...' requires an auxiliary verb, and 'can' fits the present tense and meaning.
The inversion after 'Not only' requires the auxiliary 'do' to form the present simple question form.
The structure 'Such is...that...' introduces a result clause, making 'that' the only correct choice.

record.passage: Last spring, a group of students at a local high school started a volunteer programme to help elderly people in their community. The idea came from a class discussion（讨论） about social responsibility. The students decided to visit the elderly twice（两次） a week, helping them with housework and chatting with them. At first, some students were nervous because they had never done anything like this before. However, after a few visits, they became more confident and began to enjoy the experience. One student said, "I used to think volunteering was just about giving time, but now I realise it's also about learning from others." The programme was so successful that the school decided to expand it to include more students and activities. The local government praised the students for their efforts and encouraged other schools to follow their example. The students learned that even small actions can make a big difference to someone's life.

record.passage: The Spring Festival is the most important traditional festival in China. It is a time when families come together to celebrate the new year. Before the festival, people clean their houses to sweep away bad luck and decorate doors with red couplets（对联）. On New Year's Eve, families enjoy a big dinner, and many people stay up late to welcome the new year. Children receive red envelopes with money, which is a symbol of good fortune. The festival lasts for about fifteen days and ends with the Lantern Festival. During this time, people visit relatives and friends, and they exchange gifts and good wishes. It is also a time to remember ancestors and to honour traditions that have been passed down for centuries. Many people believe that it is important to spend time with family during this festival. If someone should be unable（无法） to return home, they will still call their family to send greetings. The Spring Festival is not just a holiday; it is a celebration of family and culture. It reminds us to value our loved ones and to keep our traditions alive.

record.passage: Last spring, a group of students noticed that a piece of waste ground behind their school was covered with rubbish. They decided that the empty space should become a small city garden. Their teacher, Ms Chen, supported the plan and helped them write a letter to the local office. The students explained that a garden would give everyone a quiet place to relax and that fresh vegetables could be shared with old people nearby. After several weeks, the office agreed, and the students began to clear the ground. They worked every Friday afternoon, and by early summer the first seeds were in the soil. What surprised the whole class was how quickly the neighbours joined in. A retired teacher brought flower pots, and a classmate's father fixed an old water tap. By autumn, the garden was full of green leaves and bright flowers. Ms Chen often says that the project has taught the students more than any textbook（教科书） could. They have learned to cooperate, to keep promises, and to care for a shared space. The garden is now a small green corner in a busy city, and it reminds everyone that even a forgotten（遗忘） place can become beautiful when people work together.

record.passage: True sportsmanship（体育精神） is not about winning medals but about respect and fairness. Last year, our school held a charity basketball game. The student who organised it was a quiet girl from our class. She spent weeks training the team, yet she never asked for praise. During the game, a classmate fell and hurt his knee. The player who had the ball stopped at once and helped him up, even though this cost his team a chance to score. The crowd cheered for his kindness, not for the score. After the game, the coach said, "A true champion is one who respects others." The girl who had worked so hard smiled and said, "If I had wanted only to win, I would have felt empty. But because we helped each other, we all won." The event was covered by the local newspaper, and the story was shared online. Many students were inspired by the team's spirit. sportsmanship（体育精神）, therefore, is not just about ability; it is about character.

record.passage: Last year, the student joined the school music club. At first, she felt nervous because she had never played an instrument. Her teacher, an experienced musician（音乐家）, encouraged her to try the violin. He said that learning music is like learning a language: it takes time and patience. The student practised（熟练的） every afternoon after class. Sometimes she made mistakes, but she did not give up. A classmate, who played the piano, often practised（熟练的） with her. They shared tips and cheered each other on. After six months, the student performed in the school concert. Standing on the stage with her classmates, she felt proud. She realised that music had taught her not only how to play the violin but also how to work with others. Now she believes that anyone can learn music if they are willing to put in the effort. Music has become an important part of her life.

record.passage: In today's digital age, apps and websites collect personal information every day. Not only do they track what we buy, but they also record where we go and whom we talk to. This raises a serious question: how much privacy are we willing to give up for convenience（便利）? A recent survey asked high school students about their online habits. It found that many students share their location and photos without thinking about the risks. The survey also showed that students who had received advice from teachers were more careful about what they posted. However, only a small number of schools actually teach digital privacy. One student said that she had never considered who might see her posts until a classmate warned her. After that, she changed her account settings and stopped sharing her address. The law in many countries now requires companies to ask for permission before collecting data. Yet experts argue that the most effective protection（保护） is education. They believe that students need to learn how to manage their digital footprint（足迹） from an early age. What is the main purpose of the passage? It is to inform（告知） readers about digital privacy issues and suggest that education is key. Without proper guidance（指导）, young people may unknowingly（不知不觉） put themselves in danger. Therefore, schools and parents should work together to teach responsible online behaviour.

record.passage: Last month, a museum in our city started a new education programme for high school students. The programme, which was designed by a team of teachers and museum guides, aims to make history more alive. Students are encouraged to touch copies of ancient objects and to take part in small dramas. The student, who had never visited a museum before, said the experience changed her mind. Her teacher, who organised the visit, believes that such programmes should be offered to every school. A classmate, whose father works at the museum, helped to prepare the activities. According to the museum director, the programme has already welcomed over 500 students. If the museum had more money, it would open a second room for hands-on（实践） learning. The director suggests that the government should give more support to museum education. The museum also plans to train students as young guides. These guides, who will wear special uniforms, will lead tours for younger children. The programme is free, but booking is required. Many parents have said that their children now ask to visit museums at weekends. The museum hopes that this interest will grow into a lifelong（终身） love of learning.

record.passage: When the student first joined the school debating club, she felt nervous because she knew nobody. A classmate noticed her standing alone and invited her to sit with the team. At first, the student doubted whether she could trust anyone so quickly. However, the classmate shared her own story of feeling lost in a new school, and the student began to relax. They practised（熟练） together every Tuesday and Thursday, and slowly the student learned that trust grows through small, honest actions. One afternoon, the classmate told the student a secret about a family problem. The student promised to keep it private. The next week, another club member asked the student what she knew. She simply said, “I don’t know anything about that.” If she had shared the secret, the classmate would have been deeply hurt. Instead, the classmate later thanked her and said, “I knew I could depend on you.” From that day on, their friendship became stronger. The student realised that true friendship is not about always having fun; it is about being reliable when someone is weak. She also learned to listen without judging, and to speak up when a friend needed support. By the end of the term, the two students were leading the club together, and the student often told new members, “Trust is built slowly, but it can be broken（破碎） in a second.”

record.passage: Last month, the student felt stressed because she had too many tasks and too little time. Her teacher advised that she should make a weekly plan and focus on one thing at a time. The student decided to try this advice. On Monday, she listed all her tasks and ranked（排名） them by importance（重要性）. She put the most important task first and planned to finish it before lunch. However, a classmate asked for help with homework, and she agreed. As a result, she did not finish her own task until late afternoon. The next day, she set a timer for 25 minutes and worked without stopping. She found that she could complete more in a short, focused period than in a long, distracted one. By Friday, she had finished all her tasks and even had time to relax. She realised that time management is not about doing more; it is about doing what matters first. Now she feels more confident and less worried about deadlines（截止日期）.

record.passage: Last spring, a group of students at a small town school started a club called Friends of Wildlife. The idea came from the student who had seen a wild bird hurt by plastic waste near the river. She believed that small actions could make a big difference, so she asked her teacher for help. The teacher advised the club to focus on one clear goal: protecting local animals and their homes. Since then, the club has been working hard. Posters have been put up in every classroom, and hundreds of old batteries have been collected and sent away safely. Last month, a nature walk was organised by the students themselves, and more than fifty families joined it. The members also built small wooden（木制） boxes for birds and placed them along the river. If every student took part in such simple activities, the local environment would become much safer for wildlife. The club has also invited a scientist to give a talk. Her message was clear: it is important that everyone should respect wild animals and keep a safe distance from them. The students now understand that protection（保护） is not only the duty of experts. They hope their story will encourage other schools to act before it is too late.

Her teacher quickly set up a plan so she could keep up with the class. Every morning, the student joined a video lesson on her laptop. At first, she found it hard to focus because her little brother was often noisy（嘈杂）. However, her teacher gave her a simple tip: use headphones（耳机） and sit in a quiet corner. The student also learned to take notes during the video and to ask questions in the chat box. After a few days, she felt more confident. What surprised her most was that she could replay（重放） parts of the lesson she did not understand. This was something she could not do in a normal classroom. Her classmate, who was also learning online for a week, agreed that the recorded lessons were a big help. Not only did the student finish all her homework on time, but she also got a better score on the next test. She now believes that online learning, when used wisely, can be a useful tool for students who cannot（不能） attend school in person.

The library offers free internet access, quiet study rooms, and weekly activities such as reading clubs and craft workshops（工作坊）. These services are designed to support lifelong（终身） learning and to bring neighbours together. Not only does the library provide books, but it also hosts talks by local writers and scientists. For example, a retired teacher now volunteers to help children with their homework, and a group of teenagers has started a robotics（机器人学） club there. The building itself is bright and welcoming, with large windows and comfortable seating. It is open seven days a week, and membership is completely free. record.passage: Sustainable tourism means travel that protects nature and helps local people. It is not just a fashion. Many places in China now welcome tourists in a green way. In a small village near a mountain, the local people have turned their old houses into guest rooms. They use solar power and grow vegetables for guests. The village is not crowded, and the river is clean. The student who visited last summer said, "It was the quiet and the fresh air that made me want to stay longer." Her teacher explained that such travel brings money to the village and teaches visitors to respect the environment. However, some tourists still leave rubbish and waste water. The local government has made rules to stop this. It is the duty of every traveller（旅行者） to follow these rules. Sustainable tourism is not only about beautiful views; it is about a balance between people and nature. When we choose green travel, we help keep the earth healthy for the future.

record.passage: Stress is a common problem for high school students. Many students feel worried before exams or when they have too much homework. If a student feels stressed, it is important to take action. First, they should talk to someone they trust, like a parent or a teacher. Second, they should take breaks and do something they enjoy, such as listening to music or playing sports. Third, they should get enough sleep and eat healthy food. It is also helpful to remember that everyone feels stress sometimes. If students follow these tips, they will be able to manage stress better. However, some students ignore the signs of stress. They think that if they study harder, they will feel better. But this often makes things worse. A healthy balance between study and rest is key. Schools can also help by offering support and creating a friendly environment. Students should know that it is okay（好的） to ask for help. With the right support, every student can succeed.

The programme, which she called 'Wear Again', collects used clothes and gives them to families in need. Li Hua believes that reusing（再利用） clothes is better than making new ones because it saves resources. Not only does this programme help the environment, but it also teaches students about the value of sharing. The clothes are cleaned and sorted by volunteers every weekend. So far, over 500 items have been donated. Li Hua hopes that by recycling, we can reduce waste and protect our planet. record.passage: In 1925, the small town of Greenfield built its first public library, which quickly became the heart of the community. The library was founded by a group of local teachers who believed that books should be available to everyone, not just the wealthy. At first, the collection was tiny—only about 200 books—but it grew steadily（稳步地） as residents donated their own volumes（卷册）. The library's most dedicated（专注的） supporter was a retired teacher, who spent hours each week reading to children and helping them choose books. By 1950, the library had moved to a larger building, which was paid for by public donations. Today, the Greenfield Library stands as a reminder of how a small group of determined people can create something lasting. It is more than just a place to borrow books; it is a symbol of the town's commitment to education and community spirit. The library's current director often says that if the founders could see the modern facility, they would be amazed at how their dream has grown. However, she also reminds visitors that the library's success depends on continued support from the community, and she suggests that everyone should volunteer or donate when possible. The story of Greenfield's library shows that even the smallest efforts can lead to great achievements.

record.passage: Learning how to study efficiently is a skill that can change a student's school life. The student used to spend hours reading notes without remembering much. (2) ________. The student also learned to space out her practice. Instead of cramming（死记硬背） the night before an exam, she reviewed a little each day. (3) ________. Another habit she picked up was to remove distractions（分心）. She put her phone in another room and kept only her books on the desk. (4) ________. Finally, she made a weekly plan and stuck to it. (5) ________. Within a month, her grades improved and she felt less stressed. Efficient study habits, not longer hours, made the real difference.

options: A. This advice sounded strange at first, but she decided to give it a try.

E. Her friend borrowed her dictionary.
F. The exam was moved to next week.
G. She bought a new schoolbag.

record.passage: Planning a trip abroad can be exciting, but it also requires careful preparation. Last month, the student and her teacher discussed a journey to Singapore. The teacher advised her to make a list of things to do. (1) ______ The student wanted to visit many places, but she had only five days. (2) ______ She decided to focus on the most important sites. (3) ______ (4) ______ (5) ______ After that, she booked a hotel near the airport and packed her bags. She also learned that some items, like medicine, must be declared（声明） at customs. In the end, her careful planning made the trip smooth and enjoyable.

questions.stem: Choose the best sentence for blank (1).
options: She had already travelled to many countries before.
However, she had never planned a trip by herself.
She wanted to buy a new suitcase for the journey.
Therefore, she asked her teacher for help.
The teacher suggested a short trip to a nearby city.
She was not sure whether she needed a passport.
She decided to cancel the trip because of the cost.
questions.explanation: 前文说老师建议她列清单，后文说她只想去很多地方但时间不够，说明她缺乏独立计划旅行的经验，因此B“然而，她从未自己计划过旅行”最连贯。A和C与上下文无关，不能解释她需要老师建议的原因。主要干扰项 A 和 C 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: The teacher advised her to make a list of things to do.
questions.clue_argument: 老师建议列清单，暗示学生缺乏经验，B中的“never planned by herself”与之呼应。

questions.stem: Choose the best sentence for blank (2).
options: She had plenty of time to see everything.
She wanted to visit every attraction in the city.
However, she had only five days.
She decided to extend her stay for a month.
She was not interested in visiting any sites.
She had already visited all the places before.
She planned to travel with a large group.
questions.explanation: 前文说她想参观很多地方，后文说她决定只关注最重要的景点，因此C“然而，她只有五天”形成转折，解释了她必须取舍的原因。A和B与后文“focus on the most important sites”矛盾。主要干扰项 A 和 B 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: The student wanted to visit many places, but she had only five days.
questions.clue_argument: 时间有限与想去的景点多形成对比，C直接点明时间限制。

questions.stem: Choose the best sentence for blank (3).
options: She decided to focus on the most important sites.
She booked a flight to another country.
She forgot to bring her passport.
She bought a guidebook about Europe.
She asked her teacher to plan the whole trip.
She decided to stay at home instead.
She wanted to learn a new language.
questions.explanation: 前文说时间只有五天，后文说“After that, she booked a hotel”，因此这里应是她做出取舍的决定，A“她决定只关注最重要的景点”最符合逻辑。B和C与后文预订酒店和打包行李的顺利进程不符。主要干扰项 B 和 C 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: She had only five days.
questions.clue_argument: 时间有限，自然要选择重点景点，A是合理的决定。

questions.stem: Choose the best sentence for blank (4).
options: She packed her bags without checking the weather.
She then checked the weather forecast for her destination.
She decided to travel without a plan.
She bought a ticket for a concert.
She forgot to bring her camera.
She asked her teacher to come along.
questions.explanation: 后文说“After that, she booked a hotel”，说明前面应是另一项准备活动，B“然后她查看了目的地的天气预报”符合旅行准备的顺序。A和C与“careful planning”的主题相反。主要干扰项 A 和 C 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: After that, she booked a hotel near the airport and packed her bags.
questions.clue_argument: 预订酒店和打包是准备步骤，查看天气也是合理的前置步骤，B符合时间顺序。

questions.stem: Choose the best sentence for blank (5).
options: She decided to travel without a passport.
She also checked the customs rules for her destination.
She forgot to book a hotel.
questions.explanation: 后文提到“some items, like medicine, must be declared（声明） at customs”，因此C“她还查看了目的地的海关规定”与后文自然衔接。A和B与后文她了解海关规定的事实矛盾。主要干扰项 A 和 B 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: She also learned that some items, like medicine, must be declared（声明） at customs.
questions.clue_argument: 后文关于海关申报的信息提示她事先查看了海关规定，C是合理的准备步骤。

Option B fits the sequence of trip preparations before booking a hotel.

record.passage: Reading habits shape how we learn and grow. The student, who loves stories, reads every day. Her teacher often says that it is through reading that we open doors to new worlds. However, a classmate seldom picks up a book. The student believes it is important that her classmate should read more. (1) ______ (2) ______ (3) ______ (4) ______ (5) ______

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fits blank (1).
options: A. Reading is a waste of time for busy students.
B. Reading is not only fun but also helps us understand others.
C. Only novels are worth reading.
D. Students should read only for exams.
E. Reading is less important than sports.
F. Reading is boring for most people.
G. Reading should be avoided if it takes too long.
questions.explanation: 前文提到学生爱读书、老师强调阅读打开新世界，后文说同学很少读书，因此此处应填阅读既有趣又有益的句子，与后文形成对比。A和D都贬低阅读或过于功利，与上下文矛盾。主要干扰项 A 和 C 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: The student, who loves stories, reads every day. Her teacher often says that it is through reading that we open doors to new worlds.
questions.clue_argument: 前文强调阅读的乐趣和益处，后文转向同学不读书，需要承上启下的对比句。

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fits blank (2).
options: A. The classmate thinks reading is a waste of time.
B. The classmate reads more than anyone else.
C. The classmate prefers watching TV to reading.
D. The classmate has no books at home.
E. The classmate often visits the library.
F. The classmate enjoys reading comics.
G. The classmate reads only for school.
questions.explanation: 前文说同学很少拿起书，后文建议多读书，此处应说明同学更爱看电视而不爱阅读，形成对比。A说阅读浪费时间，与后文建议矛盾；B说同学读得最多，与“很少”矛盾。主要干扰项 A 和 B 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: However, a classmate seldom picks up a book.
questions.clue_argument: however 表转折，说明同学与爱读书的学生相反，需要具体说明其不爱阅读的表现。

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fits blank (3).
options: A. The student thinks reading is useless.
B. The student advises her classmate to read more.
C. The student never reads books.
D. The student dislikes her classmate.
E. The student wants to stop reading.
F. The student thinks TV is better.
G. The student reads only for exams.
questions.explanation: 前文说学生认为同学应该多读书，此处应是她向同学提出建议，与后文老师的话形成呼应。A和C与“学生爱读书”矛盾。主要干扰项 A 和 C 均无法与前后句形成连贯的语义衔接。
questions.context_clue: The student believes it is important that her classmate should read more.
questions.clue_argument: 学生认为同学应该多读，自然会建议同学多读书。

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fits blank (4).
options: A. The classmate finds reading very interesting.
B. The classmate is eager to read more.

D. The classmate reads every day.

G. The classmate often goes to the library.

questions.context_clue: However, a classmate seldom picks up a book.
questions.clue_argument: seldom 表明同学不爱读书，因此对阅读不感兴趣。

record.passage: Last spring, our school organised an outdoor（户外） activity in the nearby hills. The student and her classmate planned to hike to the top, but they had to change their plan because a sudden storm was coming. (1) _____, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead. While they were walking, the classmate noticed that the path was covered with fallen leaves, so they walked slowly and carefully. (2) _____, they found a small stream and stopped to rest. The student took out her camera to take photos of the beautiful scenery. (3) _____, she saw a rare bird in the trees and felt very excited. Her teacher had told them that safety should always come first, so they agreed that they should not go too far from the group. (4) _____, they returned to the meeting point before the rain started. On the way back, the student realised that the trip had been a great success. (5) _____, she learned that being prepared and working together can turn a difficult situation into a happy memory.

questions.stem: Choose the best sentence for blank (1).
options: Therefore, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead.
However, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead.
For example, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead.
In addition, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead.
As a result, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead.
Besides, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead.
Otherwise, they decided to stay near the foot of the hill and explore the forest instead.
questions.explanation: 前文说因为暴风雨要来，他们不得不改变计划，所以这里用 Therefore 表示因果关系，与后文“决定留在山脚探索森林”逻辑一致；B 项 However 表转折，与“改变计划”的因果关系不符，C 项 For example 表举例，不能连接原因和决定。
questions.evidence_sentence: The student and her classmate planned to hike to the top, but they had to change their plan because a sudden storm was coming.
questions.context_clue: The student and her classmate planned to hike to the top, but they had to change their plan because a sudden storm was coming.
questions.clue_argument: 暴风雨导致计划改变，因此用因果连接词 Therefore。

questions.stem: Choose the best sentence for blank (2).
options: However, they found a small stream and stopped to rest.

Therefore, they found a small stream and stopped to rest.

record.passage:
Learning to Communicate

Good communication is not a gift; it is a skill anyone can build. Last term, the student noticed that her group project kept failing because members rarely spoke（说话） honestly. She decided to change this.

First, she learned to listen. Instead of preparing her reply while others talked, she gave full attention to each speaker. (1) ______ This small change made classmates feel respected, and they began to share ideas more freely.

Next, she practised（练习） clear messages. She avoided long, confusing sentences and asked simple questions to check understanding. (2) ______ Only when both sides confirmed the meaning did the team move forward.

She also learned the value of tone. A message can sound rude even when the words are polite. (3) ______ Her teacher advised her to soften（软化） requests with phrases like "could you" and to thank people often.

Mistakes still happened. Once she blamed a classmate publicly, and the boy stopped speaking for days. (4) ______ If she had spoken（口语） to him privately, he would not have felt ashamed. She apologised and promised to raise problems in private.

Now the group finishes tasks on time and enjoys the work. The student believes that honest, kind talk is the bridge between people. (5) ______ If everyone learned this skill, fewer friendships would break over small misunderstandings（误解）.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fills blank (1).
options: A. She repeated their words back to show she had understood.
B. She checked her phone quietly during the meeting.
C. She interrupted whenever an idea seemed wrong.
D. She wrote down only her own suggestions.
E. She left the room without any explanation.
F. She laughed at every serious comment.
G. She refused to attend the next discussion.
questions.explanation: 空白前讲“给予每位说话者全部注意力”，后文说同学感到被尊重并更愿分享，A“复述对方的话以表示理解”承接倾听并带来尊重，最连贯。B、C 分别表示玩手机和打断别人，都与“倾听与尊重”相反，故错。
questions.evidence_sentence: Instead of preparing her reply while others talked, she gave full attention to each speaker.
questions.context_clue: This small change made classmates feel respected, and they began to share ideas more freely.
questions.clue_argument: 倾听带来尊重，需用复述确认理解的行动承接。

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fills blank (2).
options: A. She never asked anyone to explain again.
B. She sent long messages full of difficult words.
C. She asked, "Can you tell me what you understood?"
D. She decided that checking meaning was a waste of time.
E. She spoke faster so nobody could interrupt.
F. She avoided all questions during the project.
G. She told the team to guess her meaning.
questions.explanation: 前文说“用简单问题检查理解”，后文说“只有双方确认意思后才继续”，C 正是提出确认理解的问题，语义衔接紧密。A、D 都否定确认理解，与后文“确认后才推进”矛盾，故错。
questions.evidence_sentence: She avoided long, confusing sentences and asked simple questions to check understanding.
questions.context_clue: Only when both sides confirmed the meaning did the team move forward.
questions.clue_argument: 检查理解需要具体提问，C 与“确认意思”对应。

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fills blank (3).
options: A. Words alone always carry no feeling.
B. She ignored the problem completely.
C. She shouted at her teacher instead.
D. She stopped speaking to the group.
E. She decided tone did not matter at all.
F. She began to watch her tone as carefully as her words.
G. She wrote an angry note to the classmate.
questions.explanation: 空白前说“即使词语礼貌，信息也可能听起来无礼”，后文老师建议用“could you”等柔和表达并常道谢，F“开始像注意用词一样注意语气”自然承接。A、E 都否认语气的重要性，与老师建议矛盾，故错。
questions.evidence_sentence: A message can sound rude even when the words are polite.
questions.context_clue: Her teacher advised her to soften（软化） requests with phrases like "could you" and to thank people often.
questions.clue_argument: 语气会影响礼貌，因此她开始注意语气。

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fills blank (4).
options: A. Public blame helped the boy feel proud.
B. She was glad she had said it loudly.
C. The classmate thanked her for the public blame.
D. She realised her mistake at once.
E. She decided to blame him again the next day.
F. The teacher praised her for being rude.
G. She thought private talk was unnecessary.
questions.explanation: 前文说她当众责备同学，男孩几天不说话，后文用虚拟语气说“如果私下说，他就不会羞愧”，说明她意识到错误，D 最连贯。A、C 都说公开责备带来正面结果，与男孩沉默和道歉矛盾，故错。
questions.evidence_sentence: Once she blamed a classmate publicly, and the boy stopped speaking for days.
questions.context_clue: If she had spoken（口语） to him privately, he would not have felt ashamed.
questions.clue_argument: 男孩的反应与虚拟语气反思表明她认识到错误。

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best fills blank (5).
options: A. She believes silence is always the best answer.
B. She thinks misunderstandings should be ignored.
C. She now avoids all group work.
D. She feels honest talk causes more problems.
E. She has learned to keep every opinion secret.
F. She plans to stop listening to others.
G. She hopes more people will learn to speak with care.
questions.explanation: 空白前说“诚实友善的交谈是人与人之间的桥梁”，后文用虚拟语气说“如果人人都学会这项技能，更少友谊会因小误而破裂”，G“希望更多人学会用心说话”衔接顺畅。A、E 都主张沉默或隐藏意见，与“交谈是桥梁”相反，故错。
questions.evidence_sentence: The student believes that honest, kind talk is the bridge between people.
questions.context_clue: If everyone learned this skill, fewer friendships would break over small misunderstandings（误解）.
questions.clue_argument: 由“桥梁”和“人人学会”可推出她希望更多人用心沟通。

questions.reason: Option A directly follows from the context of listening and leads to the classmates feeling respected.
Option C is a specific example of asking a simple question to check understanding, matching the context.
Option F logically connects the idea of tone being important and the teacher's advice about softening requests.
Option D fits the narrative of realizing the mistake, which is supported by the following apology.
Option G aligns with the concluding thought about the importance of communication skills for everyone.
